definition: Customer Relationship Management — a system for managing interactions with current and potential customers.
extendedDefinition: CRM software centralizes customer data including contact details, communication history, and purchase records in a single accessible platform. Sales teams use CRMs to track leads, manage deals through a pipeline, and automate follow-up tasks. Marketing and support departments also rely on CRM data to personalize campaigns and resolve tickets efficiently. A well-implemented CRM strategy directly improves customer retention and revenue growth. The value depends on adoption and data discipline: teams must enter quality data and reference the system daily for the pipeline view to stay trustworthy. Mobile access, automation, and integration depth with billing and support tools decide how fully the platform serves sales and service teams. Reporting that answers pipeline and retention questions completes the picture.
description: CRM (Customer Relationship Management) software manages customer interactions, sales pipelines, and support tickets. Learn how CRM platforms improve business relationships.
